items.topic: Trap illegal vector-memory EMUL combinations before dependent assertions
items.benefit: Prevents the curated integer-vector oracle from aborting on an illegal memory instruction that should report an architectural illegal-instruction result.
items.review: The retained VLSEGTYPE, VSSEGTYPE, VLSSEGTYPE and VSSSEGTYPE clauses assert that EMUL_pow lies in [-3, 3] before their Illegal_Instruction checks. With e8,m8 and EEW64, the expression computes 6; nf=1 includes ordinary unit-stride instructions. This is a static source finding, not an executed local reproduction. Issue 1800 already covers it. Attempted PR 1828 is closed without merge and bundled the exception repair with optional NaN behavior; no matching open repair was found. The broader issue catalogue and specification-permitted NaN differences are outside this item.
items.next_action: Reproduce the retained integer-memory cases, then coordinate a narrow legality-before-assertion repair under issue 1800 with valid controls and preserved capability fault ordering.
evidence: [The curated memory clauses](../../model/model/extensions/V/vext_mem_insts.sail) retain the assertion ordering; the relevant path does not require floating-point extensions.

[The upstream diagnosis in issue 1800](https://github.com/riscv/sail-riscv/issues/1800) identifies the memory assertions. [PR 1828](https://github.com/riscv/sail-riscv/pull/1828) is closed unmerged; the current upstream source still contains the assertion ordering at observation.

Acceptance covers lower and upper invalid EMUL combinations and adjacent valid controls for each retained form, architectural state at the trap and capability permission/fault precedence. A new upstream pin alone supplies no local model qualification.

The recursive tree at upstream main c992aa61fdfe0846c5ed90324c596202a1c69b76 contains no Zicond/czero models; all-state issue/PR searches for zicond and czero each returned no match on 2026-10-22. items.next_action: Propose generator and regenerated RV32/RV64 models plus instruction-list support, and qualify them against the curated Sail clause before retiring any R2 wrapper obligation.
evidence: [The R2 smoke contract](../assurance/rtl-cosimulation-harness.md#7-the-bounded-model-checking-smoke) and [MODELS_OWED](../../tools/vos/bmc.py) explicitly name the missing conditional-zero forms.
[The curated Zicond execute clause](../../model/model/extensions/Zicond/zicond_insts.sail) supplies an independent comparison target. No upstream implementation or test was run for this proposal.

Acceptance covers both opcodes, zero/nonzero value and condition, RV64 conditions nonzero only in the upper half, rd=x0, operand/destination aliases and encoding refusal controls. Generator and generated outputs must agree. Bounded smoke evidence remains distinct from hardware refinement.

No matching repair was found among the open PRs. PR 20 restores builds and repairs return-event blame while preserving these axioms. [PR 20](https://github.com/secure-compilation/SECOMP/pull/20) is a build/theorem-maintenance change, not a soundness repair for issue 21. The ccs-main branch remains at cbef9c338d23f40db5054c9a3d6f2b3b873e9204 at observation; no independent upstream build was run.

Acceptance requires a checked composition over justified premises and the local arbitrary-context, observation, declassification and progress mapping. A repaired upstream statement alone does not establish CJ-SECOMP.

items.topic: Correct the Core 3.0 administrative-frame typing rule
items.benefit: Repairs the mandatory Core 3.0 semantic reference Q34g must curate for the first-release guest engine, before treating its administrative-frame typing rule as soundness evidence.
items.review: Open PR replaces a contradictory RETURN premise in Instr_ok2/frame with the result type installed in the inner context. Frame_ok otherwise leaves RETURN empty. Both the Core 3.0 and wasm-latest rules change; the exact semantic edition cited by the local assessment still contains the old rule. A maintainer asks whether Frame_ok itself should populate RETURN instead, so the final formulation remains under discussion. This repairs a published specification rule, not a completed Rocq Core 3.0 soundness theorem or a measured local interpreter failure.
items.next_action: Track the agreed rule formulation; Q34g must qualify the selected Core 3.0 edition and its frame/return preservation cases before consuming generated semantics or proof claims.
evidence: [Q34g’s first-release obligation](implementation-checklist.md) requires complete Core 3.0 semantics and both engine theorems; [the semantic-upstream assessment](../assurance/proof-reuse/parsers.md#other-source-leads) records that the inspected specification tree supplies no tracked Rocq proof files.

The specification edition already cited by that assessment, 95dffb694caa11c3663203f2756dda9bf24c2021, still requires C′.RETURN to equal the frame result type before checking the body in C′. The proposed repair checks the body under the explicitly extended context.

items.topic: Make memory64/table64 corpus generators exercise 64-bit indices

items.topic: Reject forged delta aliases in compiled proof libraries
items.benefit: Strengthens the independent checker trusted by R-05-018a and R-05-163 against crafted compiled libraries that give incompatible declarations the same canonical identity.
items.review: Open PR validates nontrivial serialized constant and inductive aliases against their canonical declarations before extending the checker environment. Its regressions rewrite valid compiled libraries and recompute their segment digests, then require rejection of both forgeries. This is separate from the merged resolver-substitution repair 22556 already named by R-1. VerifiedOS recompiles sources and binds cached objects by hash; no bypass of its current fresh gate was demonstrated by this review. Public platform checks do not establish a passing full upstream pipeline.
items.next_action: Track review and release/backport carriage with R-1; qualify constant and inductive forgeries, legitimate aliases and current proof-gate refusals before prover adoption.
evidence: [The proof-artifact obligations](../requirements-register.md) and [the proof gate](../../tools/README.md#current-evidence-and-generated-documentation) require independent checking and exact assumption acceptance; source and object identity remain separate controls.
[PR 22556](https://github.com/rocq-prover/rocq/pull/22556) repairs implementation delta-resolver substitution for anomaly 22555; it does not replace this serialized-alias validation.

Acceptance checks digest-recomputed constant and inductive forgeries, legitimate transparent strengthening, sealed modules and recursive/admitted roots on the qualified release. No independent upstream build or forged-object execution was run for this tracker.

items.topic: Prove and correct Bernstein-Yang generated contracts

It reports regenerated documentation with executable arithmetic unchanged. The local P256 header still claims that msat is less than the modulus it returns and specifies an odd-branch subtraction of arg4 from itself. This is a contract/proof gap, not a demonstrated arithmetic execution failure. The emission owner explicitly excludes divstep and related routines from its current vector campaign.
items.next_action: Coordinate review of the draft and narrower overlapping repairs as one work item, resolve outstanding upstream checks, and qualify discharged contracts, assumptions and exact regenerated output before extending local emission or inversion claims.

Comment repair alone supplies neither target refinement nor a complete inversion theorem.

items.topic: Exercise relaxed-dot intermediate i16 overflow
items.benefit: Strengthens Q34g’s mandatory relaxed-SIMD corpus with cases that distinguish the required intermediate truncation from a direct sum into i32.
items.review: Open PR adds boundary cases with byte operands -128, making each pair sum 32768 and exposing the i16 intermediate. For the add variant with zero accumulator, a direct-byte sum returns 65536, outside the proposed allowed lane values -65536, -1 and 65534. The existing inputs keep pair sums in range and cannot distinguish that error. The captured upstream interpreter check fails the new add-variant case with wrong return values, so the expected-result/reference disagreement remains unresolved; neither side supplies accepted local semantics. This is required guest-feature coverage; no local interpreter failure was demonstrated.
items.next_action: Resolve the failing upstream overflow case and outstanding checks, then qualify the agreed fixtures in Q34g’s shared manifest against the generation-fixed DET choices, including a control that omits the i16 intermediate.
evidence: [The complete guest-language contract](contracts/wasm-execution.md#wasm-30-inside-the-existing-boundary) includes fixed and relaxed SIMD with generation-fixed DET choices. [The shared corpus](contracts/wasm-execution.md#shared-upstream-corpus) has one feature-mapped fixture manifest.

Acceptance exercises both relaxed-dot forms, the intermediate-overflow case, nonzero accumulators and ordinary in-range controls. Each implementation must return its selected deterministic result; a broad allowed-result set must not replace the exact DET-profile check.

The upstream report describes interpreter bugs that the preceding corpus missed. [The captured interpreter log](https://github.com/WebAssembly/spec/actions/runs/32062414434/job/99852679950) reports wrong return values at relaxed_dot_product.wast lines 117-126. This tracker read that failure and the fixture diff without independently executing the reproducers or assigning the discrepancy to the test or interpreter.

items.topic: Specify signed zero for floating zero times finite nonzero
items.benefit: Closes a numeric-semantic gap in the full Core 3.0 reference Q34g must curate, including the sign of zero in ordinary floating multiplication.
items.review: Issue 2300 remains open; no matching open repair PR was found. The inspected fmul rules cover zero times infinity and zero times zero but omit zero times finite nonzero. Those cases reach ieee_N(0), whose zero rounding returns +0, so expressions such as -0 times +1 lose their required sign. The issue reports agreement among the reference interpreter and two independent runtimes on -0. This review checked the written rules but did not execute those runtimes.
items.next_action: TBD: coordinate explicit signed-zero cases under issue 2300, keeping prose and formal rules aligned, with both operand orders, signs, f32/f64 and applicable SIMD regressions.
evidence: [The numeric contract](contracts/wasm-execution.md#wasm-30-inside-the-existing-boundary) requires complete deterministic Core 3.0 numeric behavior; [the semantic-upstream assessment](../assurance/proof-reuse/parsers.md#other-source-leads) keeps the selected edition and generated proof frontier explicit.

[The upstream multiplication rules](https://github.com/WebAssembly/spec/blob/main/document/core/exec/numerics.rst#op-fmul) and issue 2300 identify the missing cases. Acceptance fixes the qualified semantic edition rather than silently changing the meaning of a pinned reference.

Acceptance covers positive/negative zero with positive/negative finite nonzero operands in both orders and widths, plus zero/zero, infinity, NaN and nonzero-underflow controls; qualify scalar rules and their fixed-SIMD consumers. No specification edit alone establishes local engine refinement.
